cards.explanation: The answer is False, and it all comes down to one little word. Peter, the apostle writing this letter, says to rid yourselves “…of all malice, deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and slander.” Not most of them, and not just the ones that are easy to give up. Every last crumb goes, friends.

The answer is milk! Peter says, “Like newborn babies, crave pure spiritual milk…” A newborn doesn't need to be talked into wanting it, and that's the picture Peter picks. The milk has a purpose too: “…so that by it you may grow up in your salvation…”

The answer is so they can grow up in their salvation. Peter says to crave the milk “…so that by it you may grow up in your salvation…” Newborns don't stay newborns, friends, and that's the whole idea. The growing comes by the milk.
The answer is True! Peter says to crave the milk “…now that you have tasted that the Lord is good.” He's talking to people who have already had a taste. That's why the craving makes sense.

The answer is chosen and precious. Peter says the living stone is “…rejected by men but chosen and precious in God’s sight…” Men rejected Him, but in God's sight He is chosen and precious. I know a little about being shoved to the back of a junk drawer and then called out of it, and it's a very good feeling.

The answer is a spiritual house! Peter says the believers, “…like living stones, are being built into a spiritual house…” In Peter's picture, believers aren't stones sitting in a pile, friends. They're being built into a building.

The answer is priesthood! Peter says the living stones are being built “…to be a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.” The house comes with a job attached. The job is offering spiritual sacrifices to God.
The answer is Jesus Christ. Peter says the sacrifices are “…acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.” The offering doesn't get its welcome from how fancy it is, friends. It comes through Him.

The answer is that they will never be put to shame! The Scripture says, “…the one who believes in Him will never be put to shame.” That's a promise worth putting on the fridge. Shame doesn't get the last word, bakers.

The answer is False. Peter says, “To you who believe, then, this stone is precious.” Then he turns to those who do not believe and speaks about them separately. So precious is how the believers see it.

The answer is because they disobey the word, and that's the reason Peter gives. He says, “They stumble because they disobey the word…” The reason is right there in the verse, so no guessing needed, friends.

The answer is a people for God's own possession. Peter says, “But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession…” Look at that list, friends. Every title is one more way of saying the believers belong to Him.

The answer is to proclaim the virtues of the One who called them! Peter says they are “…to proclaim the virtues of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.” The names come first, and then comes the job. You get to tell people what He's like.

The answer is light. Peter says God “…called you out of darkness into His marvelous light.” I understand that move from dark to bright, because an angel once called me out of a dusty junk drawer where I had sat for years.

The answer is True! Peter says, “Once you were not a people, but now you are the people of God…” That's a before and an after in one sentence, friends. Peter puts the "once" and the "now" side by side.

The answer is mercy. Peter says, “once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.” That's a before and after worth sticking on the cookie box, bakers. Once it hadn't been received, and now it has.
